# Re-entry Navigation Case Plan: Christopher Barranco

## 1. Participant Overview
Chris is a 41-year-old male with a strong background in construction, heavy machinery, and forklift operation. He is currently residing in an Oxford House (serving as President) and shows deep commitment to his faith-based recovery. However, he exhibits significant cognitive minimization regarding his criminal history (denying adult convictions and a history of DV) and has a hidden/unacknowledged active probation warrant in Kershaw County.

## 2. Immediate Stability Triage (Red Flags)
- **Active Warrant:** Chris has an active probation warrant out of Kershaw County (Dec 2025). This is an immediate threat to his stability and freedom. 
- **Financial Distress:** Chris is highly stressed about child support, debt ($3,500), and Oxford House rent. 

## 3. Case Management Strategy & CBT Integration
- **Modeling Neutrality (Standard 1.5):** Chris minimizes his past (denies adult charges/DV). Do not argue. Use reflective listening: *'Chris, I hear that you feel you've left your past behind you. I want to make sure no old records pop up to surprise employers. Let's look at this background report together and you can tell me what's going on with these items.'*
- **Managing Resistance (Standard 3.2):** Link resolving the Kershaw County warrant directly to his self-interest: *'We need to get this warrant cleared up so you don't lose your spot at Oxford House or get pulled off a high-paying construction site.'*
- **Criminogenic Targets:** Address procriminal attitudes (minimization), employment deficits, and ensure his relapse prevention plan remains robust given his history of self-sabotage (Q20).

## 4. Action Items for Navigator
1. **Legal:** Assist Chris in contacting SC Legal Services to determine the nature of the Kershaw warrant. Support him in communicating with PO Agent Burgess.
2. **Financial/Basic Needs:** Refer to Midlands Fatherhood Coalition to adjust child support based on his current unemployed status. Refer to Harvest Hope for food to save his stipend for rent.
3. **Employment:** Prep him for fair-chance industrial/heavy machinery roles. Focus on his gutter installation, Rotochopper, and forklift certifications.

# My Fresh Start Action & Resource Guide: Chris Barranco

Chris, congratulations on your leadership as President of your Oxford House and your dedication to your sobriety. You have incredibly strong skills in heavy machinery, forklift operation, and construction. This guide is designed to help you tackle your financial stress, clear up any legal roadblocks, and land a high-paying job that utilizes your talents.

## 1. Your Goals & Strengths
- **Your Vision:** To follow the Lord's will, marry your fiancée, maintain your sobriety, and secure physically demanding, high-wage work.
- **Your Strengths:** Certified forklift operator, heavy machinery experience (skid steers, Rotochopper, loaders), and a proven ability to lead in your recovery community.

## 2. Local Resource Referrals
Here are services in Columbia to help you lower your expenses and handle legal barriers:

- **SC Legal Services - Columbia Office**
  - *Why:* To help you look into and safely clear up any old court statuses or warrants (like the one in Kershaw County) so they don't threaten your freedom.
  - *Contact:* (803) 744-9430 | 2109 Bull St, Columbia, SC 29201
  - *Links:* [Visit Website](https://sclegal.org) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=2109+Bull+St,+Columbia,+SC+29201)

- **Midlands Fatherhood Coalition**
  - *Why:* They can help you with child support court representation to adjust your payments while you are job hunting, reducing your financial stress.
  - *Contact:* (803) 933-0530 | 1821 Hampton St, Columbia, SC 29201
  - *Links:* [Visit Website](https://midlandsfathers.com) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=1821+Hampton+St,+Columbia,+SC+29201)

- **Harvest Hope Food Bank**
  - *Why:* Get free emergency groceries to free up your Turn90 stipend so you can pay your Oxford House rent and reduce debt.
  - *Contact:* (803) 254-4432 | 2220 Shop Rd, Columbia, SC 29201
  - *Links:* [Visit Website](https://harvesthope.org) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=2220+Shop+Rd,+Columbia,+SC+29201)

## 3. Recommended Job Matches
Based on your heavy machinery and forklift background, here are active employers hiring now:

1. **ProLogistix / ResourceMFG Midlands**
   - **Role:** Warehouse Material Handler / Machine Operator
   - **Pay:** $17.50 – $21.50 / hr
   - **Why it fits:** Matches your prior Target Distribution Center and certified forklift experience. They are a fair-chance partner.
   - **Action:** [Apply Online](https://www.resourcemfg.com/locations/columbia-sc/?utm_campaign=resourcemfg_Branch_Listings_70325_nonpaid_3183&utm_medium=web_listing&utm_source=google)

2. **Midlands Concrete & Paving Solutions**
   - **Role:** Heavy Equipment / General Laborer
   - **Pay:** $18.00 – $23.00 / hr
   - **Why it fits:** Utilizes your heavy machinery (loaders/skid steers) and construction background. Second-chance employer.
   - **Action:** [Apply Online / View Careers](https://www.indeed.com/jobs?q=concrete+paving+laborer&l=Columbia%2C+SC)

3. **Capital City Landscaping & Site Prep**
   - **Role:** Commercial Groundskeeper / Mower Operator
   - **Pay:** $17.00 – $20.50 / hr
   - **Why it fits:** Matches your experience in landscape work, mulch manufacturing, and physical labor.
   - **Action:** [Apply Online / View Careers](https://www.indeed.com/jobs?q=commercial+landscaping&l=Columbia%2C+SC)

## 4. Your 4-Week Milestone Checklist
- [ ] **Week 1:** Call SC Legal Services to look into your Kershaw County record and discuss next steps with your Turn90 Navigator and Agent Burgess.
- [ ] **Week 2:** Contact Midlands Fatherhood Coalition to review your child support setup and get your finances organized.
- [ ] **Week 3:** Update your resume highlighting your forklift certification, gutter machine maintenance, and heavy equipment operation.
- [ ] **Week 4:** Submit applications to ProLogistix and Midlands Concrete. Practice your interview skills, focusing on how your recovery has made you a reliable worker today.

INTERVIEW TRANSCRIPT ALIGNED &
RECONSTRUCTED
Participant: Christopher David Barranco | DOB: May 7, 1985 (Age 41)
Assessment Date: August 27, 2026 | Supervision: SC Department of Probation, Parole, and
Pardon Services
TRANSCRIPT NOTE: This document represents the fully aligned, chronological, and typo-corrected interview
transcript of Christopher David Barranco. The raw digital export was affected by a systematic alignment shift
due to demographics splitting and relational merges. This official transcript has been re-indexed,
mathematically verified, and formatted for clinical and case management use.
Question 1: What is your full name, date of birth, and current address?
My full name is Christopher David Barranco. I'm born on May 7th of 1985. My current address is 200 Marabou
Circle, West Columbia, South Carolina 29169.
Question 2: What is your license status?
I have a valid driver's license. [Note: Collateral checks indicate a history of suspensions, though the participant
asserts current validity].
Question 3: What forms of ID do you have access to?
I have access to my state-issued ID and my social security card. I do not have a birth certificate with me
currently.
Question 4: How many convictions did you have as a juvenile?
I have four convictions as a juvenile. I have a lot of convictions as a juvenile, both misdemeanors and felonies. I
got in trouble a lot back then.
Question 5: How many adult convictions do you have?
Nope, none. [Note: This self-report is a total denial/minimization; collateral criminal background reports show a
dense history of forgery, petit larceny, domestic violence, child neglect, and drug possession spanning 20+
years].
Question 6: If you have pending charges, list them. If not, list original charges vs. convictions.
No pending charges. [Note: Active probation warrant is filed in Kershaw County from Dec 12, 2025; participant
has outstanding court statuses].
Question 7: At what age were you first arrested or charged with anything?
I was 11 years old when I was arrested in Coral Springs, Florida, for trespassing.

-- 1 of 7 --

CHRISTOPHER DAVID BARRANCO - INTAKE TRANSCRIPT
Page 2
Question 8: Were you ever incarcerated as a result of a conviction?
I've never been to state or federal prison, but I have spent a lot of time in County jails and I was in and out of
DJJ [Department of Juvenile Justice] as a teenager.
Question 9: Have you had any behavior reports or misconduct while in prison?
No. I've never been to prison, so I have no prison behavior reports.
Question 10: Have you ever had your probation or parole suspended or revoked?
No. [Note: Collateral records indicate multiple probation violations, including arrests on April 8, 2019 and
December 12, 2025].
Question 11: Have you ever been arrested while you were under community supervision?
Yes, I have.
Question 12: Are you currently employed?
No, I am not employed right now.
Question 13: How many months did you work a payroll job in the last 12 months?
I worked about 10 months out of the last year.
Question 14: What is the longest period of time that you have been employed for?
The longest continuous job I've held was 2 years.
Question 15: Have you ever been unemployed in the community during a 12-month period?
No, I've usually been able to work when I'm active and not relapsing.
Question 16: What is the last grade that you have successfully completed?
I went to college late and completed my Associate's Degree in Accounting at Midlands Technical College. I
graduated when I was 26.
Question 17: Have you completed a high school diploma or GED?
Yes, I completed my high school diploma before entering college.
Question 18: Have you ever been suspended or expelled?
Yes, I have a history of school suspensions during my youth.

-- 2 of 7 --

CHRISTOPHER DAVID BARRANCO - INTAKE TRANSCRIPT
Page 3
Question 19: Please give feedback on the work you have done. Did you like your
boss/coworkers?
I worked in kitchen jobs, telemarketing, and sales all the way through college. In my 30s, I learned construction,
home renovation, roofing, and siding. I am a highly skilled gutter installer. I can do anything with gutters—5-inch
and 6-inch machine operations, custom spouts, and full machine maintenance. I can also operate heavy
machinery: loaders, excavators, skid steers, front-end loaders, and a Rotochopper. I've done landscape work
and manufactured mulch from scratch with Peterbilt blower trucks. I am a former certified forklift operator and
worked at Target Distribution Center. I enjoy physically demanding work where I can earn high wages. I get
along great with bosses and coworkers when I am sober. I enjoy being a team player.
Question 20: Why did you leave any of the jobs you have had?
Every job I've ever lost was because of my own fault—relapsing. It usually starts with drinking, which leads to
drugs and partying. Then I start oversleeping my alarm, showing up late, and my work performance drops.
That's why I lose jobs.
Question 21: Are you single or in a relationship?
I'm engaged to a beautiful 37-year-old Christian Queen. Me and her follow the Lord and His will for our lives.
She's been in my corner throughout this battle against addiction. We have not set a wedding date, and we are
not going to move in with each other until we are married.
Question 22: How do you feel about being single or in a relationship?
Before I met my fiancée, I was single for almost 3 years. That was the period of greatest personal and spiritual
growth in my adult life. It was just me and God out there. Being single is very important for people to find out
who they are. If ever me and my fiancée become toxic or unhealthy, I would be willing to leave because I
understand the benefits of being single, but she is a massive blessing to me.
Question 23: Please describe your relationship with your parents.
My parents split up when I was 13. My mom left, and my dad raised me. My dad passed away in 2015, which
was a huge loss. Me and my mom are actively repairing and rebuilding our relationship now. It's a healing
process.
Question 24: Please describe your relationship with other relatives.
Me and my little brother are very tight. I love his son, my nephew Zach, to death. I am in a major rebuilding
process with all of my other relatives. Reconnecting and repairing those bonds is very important to me.
Question 25: Does anyone in your family have a criminal record?
No, I'm the criminal. Nobody else in my family has a criminal record.

-- 3 of 7 --

CHRISTOPHER DAVID BARRANCO - INTAKE TRANSCRIPT
Page 4
Question 26: What kind of organizations or clubs have you belonged to over the past year?
I'm not part of traditional clubs, but I am a very active part of the Oxford House family now. I have been involved
with Return for Christ (a faith-based rehab in Lexington) for 9 years, and I've been a dedicated member of
Calvary Chapel Lexington for 9 years. I usher and regularly cook and serve the family dinner nights there.
Question 27: How do you usually spend your free time?
I spend my free time reading my Bible, working out, meditating, watching movies, and getting rest. The Lord
has a lot of positive busyness ahead of me, and I want to be ready.
Question 28: What kind of satisfaction do you get from your free time?
If I do nothing, I sleep and can feel unproductive, but if I'm reading the Bible, working out, or doing things for my
mental health, I get a great amount of healthy, spiritual satisfaction.
Question 29: Do you know many people who have been in trouble with the law?
Historically, yes, I know a lot of people who have been in serious trouble with the law, very seriously and very
often.
Question 30: Have many of your friends been in trouble with the law?
Currently, no. I make a strict effort to surround myself with recovery peers who are trying to get their lives
together just like me. My close friends are active in recovery.
Question 31: Do you know many people who are NOT involved in crime?
Yes, I have many people in my life now who are completely uninvolved in criminal activities. They are recovery
peers and church members who have made permanent, positive changes in their lives.
Question 34: Please describe your use of alcohol and drugs.
Alcohol and drugs have plagued me since the age of 13. Even before I started using, I had to attend Al-Anon
because my dad was an alcoholic. So alcohol has been an enemy of mine since childhood. It has caused me to
waste many years of my life, but I am fully committed to my sobriety today.
Question 35: Have you had any medical problems due to drug or alcohol use?
Yes, extremely severe. I was high and drunk when I got shot in the chest, and as a result, I lost half of my left
lung. It is a constant reminder of where active addiction leads.
Question 36: Have you experienced any financial difficulties because of alcohol or drug use?
Yes, absolutely. I'm in a decent amount of debt right now because of the decisions I made while active on drugs
and alcohol.

-- 4 of 7 --

CHRISTOPHER DAVID BARRANCO - INTAKE TRANSCRIPT
Page 5
Question 37: How does your family feel about your use?
My family has historically struggled to understand my addiction. They've always known I have a lot of potential
and held me to a higher standard, so when I fell into addiction, they just didn't get it because they know I should
be doing a lot more with my life.
Question 38: How do you feel about the crimes you've committed?
I regret them deeply. I have dealt with a lot of shame and guilt for the crimes I've committed. Mentally moving
past that and accepting forgiveness has been a long and difficult process.
Question 39: Do you think the crimes were wrong?
I 100% think the crimes I committed were wrong.
Question 40: Would you like to lead a life without crime?
I would 100% like to continue leading a life without crime, as I have already started doing.
Question 41: Do you think your sentence was appropriate and fair?
Yes. Honestly, I've gotten so much mercy and grace from the courts and the Lord. I got a lot less sentencing
and prison time than I actually deserved. Praise Jesus.
Question 42: Do you think that you had a choice in getting involved in crime?
I 100% had a choice. I was misled and misguided as a youth and came from a split home, but those are not
excuses. I was making the conscious decision to do those things.
Question 43: Do you feel that the supervision you are being placed under is appropriate and
fair?
Yes, I believe supervision is appropriate and fair to help keep me and the community safe.
Question 44: Have you ever been assessed by a psychiatrist or psychologist?
Yes, I have been assisted by a psychologist recently.
Question 45: Were you ever removed from your home by DSS when you were young?
No, I was not.
Question 46: Did you ever run away from home?
Yes, I did run away as a teenager after my parents split.
Question 47: Did your parents have a lot of trouble raising you?
Yes, they did. I was very difficult and was in and out of DJJ.

-- 5 of 7 --

CHRISTOPHER DAVID BARRANCO - INTAKE TRANSCRIPT
Page 6
Question 48: Do you have any convictions for violent offenses?
No, I do not. [Note: Intelius shows historical charges of Domestic Violence 1st (2010), Domestic Violence 2nd
(2019), and Assault & Battery 3rd degree (2014)].
Question 49: Have you had any history of escape or attempted escape?
No, I have never tried to escape from any facility.
Question 50: What are the sources of Income for your household?
I don't have a job right now, so I receive no direct payroll income. I receive food stamps, and I get a small
stipend from Turn 90 which helps out, but it is not enough to cover my basic needs and debts.
Question 52: Are you worried about having sufficient money to pay debts?
I am very worried. I am in a pretty decent amount of debt over my head and have no active income.
Question 53: Do you have a bank account?
No, I do not have a bank account. PayPal is the only thing I have to do banking.
Question 54: Do you know your credit score?
The last time I checked, my credit score was in the 500s. It needs to be a lot better.
Question 55: Have you had calls or letters from creditors?
Yes, I've had a lot of phone calls from creditors requesting payments.
Question 56: Do you have any existing debts?
Yes, I owe about $3,500 to Landmark in Lexington. I need to pay them.
Question 57: Do you have a personal budget?
I don't have a personal budget in place yet, only because I am not receiving any steady money. When I do have
income, I follow budgets very well.
Question 59: Are you worried about basic needs?
Very worried. My Turn 90 stipend helps, but it is not enough to cover rent at Oxford House, child support, legal
fees, and hygiene/food.
Question 60: What is your current living situation?
I live in an Oxford House sober living situation. I like it a lot. I was actually elected the President of the house by
my peers, and things are going very well.

-- 6 of 7 --

CHRISTOPHER DAVID BARRANCO - INTAKE TRANSCRIPT
Page 7
Question 61: Is your probation officer fair and reasonable?
Yes, my agent Burgess is very reasonable.
Question 62: Are you afraid of anyone harming you?
No, I am not afraid of anyone harming me.
Question 63: Do you often act before thinking?
Historically, yes, I have done that my whole life. I am working very hard to start thinking and praying before
making decisions or acting.
Question 64: Do you set goals and make plans?
Yes, I set goals, make plans, and actively check my phone to make sure I am tracking and following those
plans.
Question 68: Do you get into trouble almost by accident?
Yes, sometimes it feels like that, but I'm learning to be more mindful.
Question 73: Have you ever physically hurt your partner?
Yes, I have in the past. [Note: This aligns with his 2010 and 2019 domestic violence charges in Lexington
County].
Question 103: Is there anything else that will hinder or hold back your progress?
I am very mindful that I am my own worst enemy. Only I can stop myself. I need to stay vigilant, maintain my
recovery, and avoid environments where people are using drugs.

-- 7 of 7 --
